exam.general: 28 year old woman at 26 weeks gestation, comfortable at rest, mild ankle oedema
exam.jvp: Normal at rest, rises on exertion
exam.other: Foetal growth normal on antenatal scan, no obstetric complication noted

history.a: Breathless on routine housework since the second trimester, first pregnancy
Sleeps on two pillows now, no waking gasps
Rheumatic fever at 12, irregular penicillin for two years then stopped
No palpitation, no haemoptysis, no chest pain
history.q: Palpitation, blood in sputum, chest pain

history.a: Takes iron and calcium, no cardiac drugs
First antenatal echo, murmur noted at booking
Husband supportive, plans delivery at the district hospital

keyPoints: Manage jointly with obstetrics and cardiology with monthly review and growth scans
Control heart rate with a beta blocker where needed to lengthen diastole, per the ESC valvular and pregnancy guidance
Use diuretics cautiously for congestion while preserving placental perfusion
Plan vaginal delivery with assisted second stage and endocarditis aware peripartum care
Defer valvotomy to after delivery unless refractory failure supervenes, then consider balloon valvotomy at a referral centre
management.model: Joint cardiac obstetric care with rate control, cautious diuresis, assisted vaginal delivery, and postpartum intervention planning

stem: A 28 year old woman at 26 weeks gestation from Nagpur, with childhood rheumatic fever, develops exertional breathlessness in the second trimester. A loud first sound with an opening snap and a grade 2 diastolic rumble is heard.
teaching: Pregnancy unmasks moderate stenosis because cardiac output rises against a fixed orifice
Sinus rhythm with broad notched P waves is the window for rate control before atrial fibrillation supervenes
Area 1.0 to 1.5 sq cm with gradient 5 to 10 mmHg is the moderate band to memorise
Assisted vaginal delivery with joint cardiac obstetric care is the standard plan
title: Moderate mitral stenosis unmasked by pregnancy
